thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert created for high GPU queue growth and failed autoscale (3409876543)

deploy-bot: ALERT: gpu-serve-pool queue_length=312, p95_latency=2.8s, available_gpus=2, pending_requests=290 :rotating_light:

luke: ack, i'm oncall. seeing autoscaler logs: "scale attempt failed: reached max_nodes (limit=120)". also a bunch of pod Pending due to scheduling. paging maya for capacity/placement help @maya

maya: on it. quick question — is this a single region or multi-region fail?

luke: single region (us-west2). load spike landed ~3409876400, queue started climbing at ~3409876500. autoscale tried to add nodes but kept failing to place pods: "No nodes are available that match the Pod's constraints"

ana: past incident pattern: when MIG sizes don't match request shapes we get fragmentation. can someone paste `kubectl describe pod` for one Pending?

jordan: pasted: ```
Name: gpu-serve-xyz-abc
Status: Pending
Message: 0/48 nodes are available: 35 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 13 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector.
```

luke: also seeing scheduler logs with "InsufficientResource: pod requests 8gpus, node has 4gpus (MIG slices)". looks like new model shards request larger MIG than available slices.

maya: that matches — recent rollout changed default `gpu_request` from 4 -> 8 for the v2 runner. bins are now incompatible with many nodes that are MIG-sliced to 4. we effectively stranded a lot of capacity.

sam (support): customer impact: support telemetry shows 14 customer apps with >30% error rate (502/timeout) starting 5m ago. on a call with key account A, they're seeing retries.

luke: mitigation plan attempt 1: temporarily lower model runner gpu_request to 4 for new replicas to fit existing MIG slices. Jordan, can you patch deployment to v2-hotfix?

jordan: patching now: `kubectl set env deployment/gpu-serve RUNTIME_GPU_REQ=4 --record`

infra-bot: Note: changing gpu_request may cause memory OOMs if model larger than slice. Please monitor OOMKilled.

ana: agree. parallel mitigation: trigger emergency-rebalance to consolidate free 4-gpu slices into nodes that can host 8-gpu pods later. but rebalance will cause transient evictions.

maya: can we also temporarily bump autoscaler max_nodes to 200 to allow more raw capacity if needed? current account limits are cloud quota; need infra approval.

luke: i'll request quota increase via infra channel, but that will take time. let's do the software-side fixes first.

jordan: patch applied. new replicas are spinning up, some immediately scheduled onto 4gpu-slices. queue dropping from 312 -> 180 in the last 2m.

sam (support): updating customers: "We're aware of degraded API performance; engineers are mitigating; ETA 30-60m."

maya: starting emergency-rebalance (dry-run=false). Command: `./ops/rebalance --pool gpu-serve-pool --strategy pack` (this will try to consolidate fractional MIG slices). Expect 2-5m of evictions.

deploy-bot: Rebalance job started (job_id=rb-2026-03-15-01).

luke: observed autoscaler errors: `failed to place pods due to binpacking conflicts, fractional resources reserved by stale allocations`. Looks like node-level reservations from older orphaned pods. I'll kick garbage collector on GPU resource leases.

infra-bot: GC triggered: `gc_gpu_leases --pool gpu-serve-pool --older-than 15m`

jordan: rebalance finished. outcome: 42 nodes drained & repacked, 38 nodes repopulated with consolidated full-GPU nodes, freed_slices=96. some pods restarted.

maya: after repack, available_gpus=46, queue=92, p95_latency=1.4s. still throttling because some long-running requests are draining KV cache.

luke: note: we had two constraints contributing: 1) default runner gpu_request bumped to 8 (workflow change) 2) large fraction of fleet had MIG configured to 4 due to older rollout. combo -> fragmentation.

ana: next steps (short): 1) rollback any non-critical rollout that increased gpu_request (done) 2) run fleetwide MIG audit to align slice sizes with current defaults 3) add a scheduler predicate to allow flexible placement across MIG sizes when safe.

maya: i pushed a temporary scheduler policy allowing 8->4 fallback placement if container has `flexible_placement=true`. will monitor for regressions.

sam (support): customers reporting errors down to 6 apps now, message updated: "We've reduced impact significantly; background work ongoing."

luke: handing over to maya for next shift (handoff_ts=3409878920). Summary: initial cause = MIG/requests mismatch + stale reservations; mitigations = lower gpu_request, emergency rebalance, gc leases, scheduler fallback. Current status: degraded -> partial recover. Please keep monitoring queue <100 and p95 <2s.

maya: thanks, taking over. I'll keep this thread updated. @sam please ping me if any major customer escalations. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident P1 status changed -> Monitoring, assignee=maya, incident_duration=47m
